When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
These 2 questions belong together and follow one another in the test booklet.

## Question 1

There are 10 girls and 20 boys in Juanita's class. Juanita said that there is one girl for every two boys. Her friend Amanda said that means 1/2 of all the students in the class are girls.

How many students are there in Juanita's class?
Answer: ____

Is Juanita right? Answer: ____
Use words or pictures to explain why.

## Question 2

There are 10 girls and 20 boys in Juanita's class. Juanita said that there is one girl for every two boys. Her friend Amanda said that means 1/2 of all the students in the class are girls.

How many students are there in Juanita's class?
Answer: ____

Is Amanda right? Answer: ____
Use words and pictures to explain why.

Answer each of the 2 questions.

answer_1.description: Your answer to question 1, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer_1.title: Answer 1

answer_2.description: Your answer to question 2, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer_2.title: Answer 2

output.answer_1: Answer: 30 students. Answer to whether Juanita is right: Yes. Explanation: The class has 10 girls and 20 boys, so the ratio of girls to boys is 10 to 20, which is the same as 1 girl to 2 boys. Picture: Draw a row of groups, each with 1 girl (circle) and 2 boys (squares). Ten such groups make 10 girls and 20 boys, so every girl has two boys for her in the drawing.
output.answer_2: Answer: No, Amanda is not right. Explanation: The class has 10 girls out of 30 students, and 10/30 = 1/3, not 1/2. Half of the 30 students would be 15 girls. Picture: Draw 30 small squares in 3 equal rows of 10. Shade the first row of 10 for the girls. The shaded part is 1 of the 3 equal parts, which shows one third of the class, not one half.
